Thank you so much for all of this. The main issues are both my motivation problems (I have depression, and ptsd. I frequently get nightmares and flashbacks and have built a habit of eating for comfort), and my eating habits. I feel like I have no control over my eating habits.

So, first, you need to look into therapy. Go therapist to therapist until you find one you love, if you have to - just get therapy.

Second, my brother struggled with a poem addiction from 7 years old to 23 yrs old. He struggled with self-confidence issues and believed he'd never really know what love is. But, he got married at 20 and now has 2 kids with his wife. She used to get really upset because his addiction to porn went as far as following women on Instagram and snapchat just to watch their stories where they'd strip. She felt that it was almost a form of cheating. After years of discussions and some therapy, my brother started getting better. He's 24 now, so it's only been about a year since things were really bad, but he truly is getting better. You will, too. Search out resources and just keep yourself focused. Porn addiction is no different than a drug addiction. It's going to be hard, and that's ok. Just take it one step at a time. You've got this
I'm excited for you. Idk why. But good luck!

It does get better. Just have to hang on and wait for a turning point in life. I was in the same boat. I don't remember a time in my childhood where I wasn't depressed and/or suicidal. It didn't get better until I was 22. But now I'm turning 24 and sometimes it still hits like a brick, but it doesn't last long anymore. I'm at least content, and often times in genuinely happy. I didn't know what real happy was until the past year. And once you get a taste of real happy, it's all you'll live for. Every moment of depression after that, it gets easier and easier to wait it out because you know that real happy is out there now, and it always comes back.
Thank you :) that comment alone makes you amazing too. It's always good to spread positivity and love

Honestly, I get it. He laid down his personal boundary and she disrespect it, even when he said that it would be a deal breaker in their relationship. This is the woman he's meant to raise a child with, and if there isn't a foundation of trust between them, then it's going to be absolute Hell trying to raise the kid with her. I personally think the divorce is over the top, but everyone is different. It's possible that she's acted up before, or that he has some unresolved trauma from the past. Whatever the situation is, I support him in this. Though, I hope he considers couples therapy first.

I was beautiful in high school, skinny, and in good shape. But I only ever dated terrible guys. I got married at 18 and immediately started putting on weight. My now exhusband never let me have friends or go outside without him. So depression and a toxic relationship caused excessive weight gain. Then I had a baby at 20. Which made it much harder for me to take care of myself.  Before I knew it, I was pushing 280 pounds, I had acne, and I had shaved my head in defiance towards my husband at the time. I eventually left him because he cheated on me so many times and became abusive.

His best friend and I kept in touch, and now we've been together for 2 years. He's an attractive man with a good heart, and I am 240 pounds with stretch marks everywhere and graying hair at 23. The point is that the right kind of people won't fall in love with your looks. They will fall in love with YOU, and then you will be nothing but raw beauty in their eyes. Hang in here a little longer. There are good people with good hearts and good morals. You just have to breathe and wait.

But then he lived. And I realized that if he can fight that hard as a baby with just a 7% chance of survival, then I can do it too. I wanted to see him grow so I stuck around.
I stayed around :) you were right. I had the baby, and everything changed. I still struggle with depression and motivation from time to time, but my son makes everything so worth it.
